children: Morocco's central bank kept its benchmark interest rate at 2.25% on Tuesday, saying current borrowing costs were in line with the inflation outlook, despite heightened global economic uncertainty.
Inflation will average 0.7% in 2026, following a drop in food prices, before ticking up to 1.5% next year, the bank said in a statement following its quarterly board meeting.
The bank expects Morocco's energy bill to surge 28.4% to 138 billion dirhams ($14.5 billion), driven by disrupted markets due to the war in the Middle East.
However, the impact of energy prices on inflation would remain "limited", it said, citing subsidies to keep public transport, cooking gas and electricity prices stable.
Morocco's current account deficit would widen to 4.6% of GDP this year, from 2.4% last year, the bank said.
The deficit would be mitigated by higher automotive sector and fertiliser exports as well as an increase in tourism revenue.
Morocco's foreign exchange reserves are seen growing to 515 billion dirhams ($54 billion) by 2027, enough to cover 5.5 months of import needs, the central bank said.
